claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with relatively coarse dual-phase fcc/B2 lamellar colonies.
Internal phase boundaries in the as-cast lamellar colonies serve as microcrack-initiation sites.
Cryo-rolling followed by warm rolling and annealing will refine and homogenize the fcc/B2 lamellar structure.
The proposed treatment will reduce lamellar spacing and enhance connectivity between the fcc and B2 phases.
Finer lamellar spacing increases the ability of the ductile fcc phase to absorb strain.
Coherent interfaces between the fcc and B2 phases promote crack deflection or arrest.
The B2 phase is sufficiently hard to sustain high loads during tensile deformation.
The combined strain accommodation, crack deflection, and load-bearing effects delay microcrack initiation and propagation.
Delaying microcrack initiation and propagation improves both strength and ductility.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have higher yield strength than the conventionally cast baseline.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have higher ultimate tensile strength than the conventionally cast baseline.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the conventionally cast baseline.
Coarse lamellar internal boundaries facilitate premature microcracking in unmodified eutectic HEAs.
Unmodified coarse-lamellar eutectic HEAs have limited ductility despite adequate strength.
The proposed improvement is expected in eutectic HEAs with a controllable composite fcc/B2 microstructure.
The improvement may not occur when alloy composition deviates significantly from the eutectic system.
The improvement may not occur if processing fails to produce a refined, well-connected lamellar architecture.
The magnitude of strength and ductility enhancement depends sensitively on processing details and alloy composition.
A fine lamellar fcc/B2 eutectic HEA can combine high fracture strength with high ductility.
